Working at NLR

NLR is located at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains in Golden, Colorado is the nation's primary laboratory for energy systems research and development.

Join the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR), where world-class scientists, engineers, and experts are accelerating energy innovation through breakthrough research and systems integration. From our mission to our collaborative culture, NLR stands out in the research community for its commitment to an affordable and secure energy future. Spanning foundational science to applied systems engineering and analysis, we focus on solving complex challenges to deliver advanced, secure, reliable, and cost-effective energy solutions. Our work helps strengthen U.S. industries, support job creation, and promote national economic growth.

At NLR, you'll find a mission-driven environment supported by state-of-the-art facilities, multidisciplinary research teams, and strong collaborations with industry, academia, and other national laboratories. We offer robust professional development opportunities, and a competitive benefits package designed to support your career and well-being.

Job Description

The Integrated Modeling and Economic Analysis Group develops and applies energy and economic models to evaluate and inform the evolution of the energy system and the associated implications for the economy, environment, and society. We are looking forward to welcoming a new researcher to our team to contribute to a growing body of research evaluating alternative pathways to satisfy increasing energy demand from the US economy.

Working with senior researchers, the successful candidate will assist with data management and complementary coding for the Fuels and Industry Integrated Optimization (FINITO) model—a new model simulating the evolution of the US industrial and fuel supply sectors—with applications towards a range of research topics, including:

- evaluation of the implications of alternative policy designs for energy technologies,
- evaluation of effects of research and development (R&D) driven improvements to the cost and performance of energy technologies,
- evaluation of how energy changes in the industrial sector would interact with other energy sectors (e.g., electricity),
- explore impacts of different manufacturing energy decisions on US manufacturing competitiveness.

In particular, the intern will contribute to identifying, synthesizing, and implementing new data within the FINITO modeling structure; editing processing scripts; coordinating data workflow and updates; visualizing data via Tableau. In addition, the intern will assist in communication products, including presentations to deliver at workshops/conferences, technical articles for submission to peer-reviewed journals, as well as shorter written products for policy audiences.

The ideal candidate will have a high level of enthusiasm to expand one’s knowledge of the energy system, learn new skills, and apply such knowledge and skills to help identify how the US can increase energy choices while decreasing environmental impacts. We welcome applicants pursuing advanced degrees from any field, but a strong applicant must have experience developing and applying python scripts and a solid background in data management and analysis.

General job duties include:

- Assist in research that generates independent, high quality, and reproducible results,
- Research, acquisition, and analysis of complex datasets requiring substantial pre-processing and harmonization,
- Assist in development of new data architectures to flexibly describe infrastructure systems,
- Assist in executing scenarios and visualizing, analyzing, and interpreting results,
- Assist senior researchers in the design, implementation, and reporting of the research project,
- Contribute to technical reports, journal articles, and presentations.

.

WWM Logistics, LLC is seeking a Data Science Intern to support its natural gas trading desk. This role sits at the intersection of daily market reporting and deeper quantitative analysis, providing traders with the timely fundamental data they need to evaluate supply and demand, while also partnering with the Data Scientist and Strategist on model development aimed at generating trading signals. This is an ideal opportunity for a detail-oriented, quantitatively skilled early-career professional looking to build a career in commodity trading and market analytics.

This role is the natural next step for graduates of WWM's Natural Gas Analyst / Data Science Internship. Completion of the internship is valued but not required – we also hire directly into this role.

Responsibilities:

Daily Fundamentals Reporting

- Build, maintain, and deliver standardized daily reports summarizing natural gas supply and demand fundamentals (production, storage, weather-driven demand, pipeline flows, rig counts) used directly by traders to inform positioning

- Own the rollout of these standardized reports and monitor them on an ongoing basis, troubleshooting data issues and refining processes to reduce manual turnaround time and improve reliability

- Monitor and flag material shifts in fundamental data that could influence price movement, escalating findings to traders and senior analysts in real time

- Maintain data integrity across multiple third-party and internal data sources (e.g., EIA, pipeline bulletin boards, weather services, production estimates)

Modeling & Analytics

- Partner with the Data Scientist and Strategist to develop and refine quantitative models aimed at identifying trading signals from fundamental and market data

- Support back-testing and validation of new analytical approaches, helping translate research into production-ready tools

- Assist in building supply/demand balance models and scenario analyses across key basins and pipeline systems

- Contribute to the automation and scaling of data pipelines that feed both daily reporting and longer-term research projects

Cross-Functional Support

- Collaborate with traders to understand evolving information needs and adjust reporting/modeling priorities accordingly

- Support ad hoc analysis requests tied to specific trading opportunities, contract structuring, or market events

- Document methodologies and maintain clear version control across reporting and modeling tools

Qualifications:

Required

- Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field, preferably a May 2028 grad.

- Working knowledge of SQL and Python or similar language for data analysis

- Demonstrated interest in commodity markets, trading, or energy fundamentals (coursework, internships, trading simulations/competitions, or independent projects)

- Excellent attention to detail and ability to manage recurring deliverables under time pressure

- Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to translate technical analysis for a trading audience

- WhiteWater does not offer housing. Position is required to be in-office at our Austin location

Preferred

- Prior completion of WWM's Data Science Internship, or equivalent internship experience in energy trading, fundamentals, or data analytics

- Master's degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Mathematics, or a related quantitative field

- Experience with data visualization tools (Power BI, Tableau)

- Prior exposure to natural gas or broader energy markets

- Experience with trading simulations, mock portfolios, or derivatives strategy

- Ability to think critically and explain technical work to other colleagues

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible.

Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.

What you’ll do

As an intern at Stripe you’ll work on projects across our stack that directly impact the way millions of businesses operate. You’ll own problems end to end with the support of your manager and teammates. It’s an opportunity to work alongside some of the most creative and technically rigorous engineers in the industry and learn how to ship high-quality work at scale. By contributing to Stripe’s codebase you’ll work across domains that give you insight into how the global economy works. Recent intern projects include expanding Stripe’s Payments Foundation Model capabilities to improve generalized anomaly detection, building more approachable fraud controls, creating safer payouts, and developing user-facing solutions that prevent costly pricing mistakes and make merchant checkout setup easier.

Our internship program is competitive and the expectations are high.

Responsibilities

- Operate as a real member of the team you join; engage in team discussions, decisions, and the technical design process.

- Write software that will be used in production, and has meaningful impact to Stripe’s business and users.

- Give and receive technical feedback through code reviews or design discussions

- Collaborate with other engineers and cross-functional stakeholders to proactively seek and incorporate feedback.

- Learn quickly by asking great questions, working with your intern manager and teammates effectively, communicating the status of your work clearly, and building with the latest AI tooling.

Who you are

- Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty.

- Rigorous thinker: You appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. You enjoy working on problems that have never been tackled before.

- Adaptable problem solver: You adapt quickly and treat obstacles as opportunities. At Stripe we embrace kindness while encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus.

Minimum requirements

- A strong fundamental understanding of computer science through pursuit of a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in computer science, math, or a related discipline.

- Experience and familiarity with programming, either through side projects or classwork. We work mostly in Ruby, Java, Javascript, Go, and Scala. We believe new programming languages can be learned if the fundamentals and general knowledge are present.

- Experience from previous internships or other multi-person projects, including open source contributions, that demonstrate evaluating and receiving feedback from mentors, peers, and stakeholders.

- Ability to learn unfamiliar systems and form an understanding of those systems, through independent research and working with a mentor or subject matter experts.

- Ability to leverage AI tools to accelerate development while applying rigorous critical thinking and professional judgement to review, refine, and validate all outputs.

Preferred qualifications

- At least 1 year of university education, or equivalent work experience.

- One or more areas of specialized knowledge (frontend, backend, infrastructure or other technologies) balanced with general skills and knowledge.

- Experience writing high quality pull requests, with good test coverage, and working knowledge to complete projects with minimal defects.

- Familiarity with navigating and managing your work in new code bases, with multiple languages.

- Clear written communication skills, with the ability to write clearly to explain your work to stakeholders, team members, and other Stripes.

Accelerates EV Hardware Development: Developing custom automation scripts for Cadence tools eliminates repetitive manual tasks in schematic entry and routing, significantly speeding up the design cycles for Rivian's complex electronic control units.

Reduces Costly Manufacturing Errors: Automated design rule checks and standardized component generation minimize human error in critical PCB layouts, preventing expensive hardware respins for high-stakes systems like battery management and infotainment.

Optimizes Senior Engineering Bandwidth: Dedicating a Coop to build these specialized workflow tools frees up Rivian's senior hardware engineers to focus on core vehicle innovation and architecture rather than daily CAD tool management.

Responsibilities

- Develop Custom Automation Scripts: Write and deploy SKILL, Python, and TCL scripts within Cadence Allegro and OrCAD to eliminate manual data entry during schematic capture and board routing.

- Integrate ECAD/MCAD Workflows: Create automated bridges between Cadence tools and mechanical CAD software to ensure accurate, real-time synchronization of complex EV packaging constraints and board outlines.

- Enhance Component Library Management: Build tools to automatically generate, verify, and update PCB footprint and schematic symbol libraries by syncing directly with Rivian’s Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) database.

- Implement Advanced Rule Checking: Program custom Design Rule Checks (DRCs) tailored to Rivian's high-voltage and high-speed signal integrity requirements, preventing manufacturing errors before tape-out.

- Deploy and Document Toolchains: Package the developed automation tools into user-friendly interfaces, write technical documentation, and train the hardware engineering team to adopt the new workflows.

Qualifications

- Must be currently pursuing a bachelors or masters degree at an accredited university.
- Actively pursuing a degree or one closely related in computer science, electrical engineering, mechatronics, or similar.

- Possesses strong programming fundamentals with proficiency in Python, TCL, or C++, alongside an aptitude for learning proprietary EDA languages like Cadence SKILL.

- Demonstrates foundational knowledge of schematic capture and PCB layout processes, ideally with academic or project experience using Cadence OrCAD, Allegro, or similar ECAD platforms.

- Understands core hardware design principles, including component lifecycle management, basic signal integrity, and standard manufacturing constraints.

- Exhibits strong problem-solving skills with a track record of personal projects or coursework focused on software automation, API integration, or streamlining repetitive technical workflows.

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Strategic Engagement and Events Team

Strategic Engagement and Events helps Zipline build relationships, understanding, and momentum with the people who matter most to our growth. We work across Commercial, Government Affairs, Communications, Market Entry, Operations, Partnerships, and other teams to turn important business priorities into thoughtful stakeholder experiences and engagement strategies. Our work can range from hosting government and civic leaders for technology demonstrations, to supporting a new market launch, coordinating a strategic partner moment, or creating an experience for investors, customers, or community leaders. We focus on the objective first: understanding who we need to reach, what we want them to understand or do, and designing the right engagement to help make that happen. Because our work sits at the intersection of strategy and execution, our team gets a unique view into how Zipline grows and builds trust in new and existing markets.

The Role

As a Strategic Engagements & Events Intern, you’ll help turn Zipline’s biggest business moments into meaningful experiences for the people who can help move our mission forward. You’ll work alongside the Strategic Engagement & Events team from the earliest stages of an opportunity—researching audiences and markets, helping develop engagement recommendations, and building project plans—all the way through execution and follow-up. Depending on the project, you might help prepare for a visit from government leaders, support a market launch, coordinate a partner event, or help bring Zipline’s technology to life for an entirely new audience. You’ll collaborate with teams across the company and gain firsthand experience in stakeholder engagement, communications, project management, event production, and business strategy. This is a role for someone who is excited to think critically, stay organized, and roll up their sleeves to make ambitious ideas happen.

What You'll Do

- Research markets, stakeholders, and opportunities to help the team understand who we should engage, why an opportunity matters, and how it connects to Zipline’s broader business priorities.

- Help develop engagement strategies and briefing materials, including audience research, stakeholder profiles, experience concepts, agendas, talking points, and recommendations for internal teams.

- Support planning and execution of strategic engagements such as VIP visits, technology demonstrations, partner events, market launches, community activations, conferences, and company-owned events.

- Build and maintain project plans and workbacks, helping coordinate timelines, owners, guest lists, logistics, communications, production needs, and other dependencies across teams.

- Partner with teams across Zipline including Government Affairs, Communications, Commercial, Operations, Partnerships, Workplace, Design, and others to gather information and keep projects moving.

- Support onsite execution, helping create thoughtful, well-run experiences for guests and solving problems as they arise.

- Measure and document what worked, capturing outcomes, stakeholder follow-up, lessons learned, and reusable resources that make future engagements more effective.

What You'll Bring

- You are currently pursuing an undergraduate degree or have recently graduated and are excited to build experience in areas such as communications, business, marketing, public affairs, events, hospitality, or a related field. We care more about how you think and work than your specific major. Masters and PhD students are also eligible.

- You are an excellent communicator and can turn research or a collection of inputs into clear, concise written materials.

- You are highly organized and enjoy keeping track of details, deadlines, and moving pieces while maintaining sight of the larger objective.

- You are curious and analytical—you like learning about new audiences, markets, and business problems and asking thoughtful questions before jumping to a solution.

- You are comfortable taking initiative, working through ambiguity, and switching between strategic thinking and hands-on execution.

- You are collaborative and excited to work with people across many different functions, backgrounds, and levels of the organization.

- You are willing to support in-person engagements and events, which may occasionally require travel or work outside standard business hours.

What Else You Should Know

This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January to April. Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position.

The hourly rate for this internship is $34 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.

Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period.

NLR is located at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains in Golden, Colorado is the nation's primary laboratory for energy systems research and development.

Join the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR), where world-class scientists, engineers, and experts are accelerating energy innovation through breakthrough research and systems integration. From our mission to our collaborative culture, NLR stands out in the research community for its commitment to an affordable and secure energy future. Spanning foundational science to applied systems engineering and analysis, we focus on solving complex challenges to deliver advanced, secure, reliable, and cost-effective energy solutions. Our work helps strengthen U.S. industries, support job creation, and promote national economic growth.

At NLR, you'll find a mission-driven environment supported by state-of-the-art facilities, multidisciplinary research teams, and strong collaborations with industry, academia, and other national laboratories. We offer robust professional development opportunities, and a competitive benefits package designed to support your career and well-being.

Job Description

NLR's Advanced Building Equipment Research group has an immediate opening for a graduate intern position focusing on modeling and experimental heat and mass transfer applied to HVAC systems and buildings. The successful candidate will join team members on cutting-edge laboratory and analytical projects to research, develop, and evaluate heat and mass transfer components and systems, including conventional and non-conventional dehumidification and desiccant systems. The successful candidate should have a strong background and understanding of heat and mass transfer, including theory, numerical modeling, and experiments.

Under the general direction of senior staff, the successful candidate will:

• Improve and utilize existing numerical models of heat and mass exchangers

• Design, develop, and analyze new HVAC processes and components.

• Perform laboratory experiments on fluid/thermal components,

• Publish papers in heat and mass transfer and energy journals.

.

Minimum of a 3.0 cumulative grade point average.

Undergraduate: Must be enrolled as a full-time student in a bachelor’s degree program from an accredited institution.

Graduate: Must be enrolled as a full-time student in a master’s degree program from an accredited institution.
Post Graduate: Earned a master’s degree within the past 12 months. Eligible for an internship period of up to one year.
Graduate + PhD: Completed master’s degree and enrolled as PhD student from an accredited institution.

Demonstrated experience in some or all of the following:

· Heat and mass transfer fundamentals

· HVAC fundamentals or refrigeration cycles (vapor compression and non-vapor compression)

· Numerical modeling techniques and computer programming

· Familiarity with desiccants and absorption processes

· Laboratory experiments and data acquisition systems

· Experience programming in MATLAB (preferred), Engineering Equation Solver (EES), Python, or similar tools

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Commercial Implementation Team

The Commercial Implementation team plays a critical role in ensuring the successful launch and ongoing success of Zipline’s commercial operations. The team defines commercial workflows and compliance processes, tests and validates new features and procedures at test sites and partner sites, creates training materials and onboarding playbooks, and identifies and addresses operational gaps to deliver a smooth and successful P2 experience for all commercial operations. The Commercial Implementation team is deeply knowledgeable in every step of the process from order placed to successful delivery, and works with internal and external partners to optimize the experience for operators and customers.

We build the processes against which our teams and our Partners’ teams will execute operating the Zipline Network.

Commercial Implementation team members work across all Zipline partner verticals and test sites. Site launch, training, and ownership will be determined by a combination of partner type and location.

The Role

As Project Manager on the Commercial Implementation team you will focus on designing, optimizing, and maintaining the workflows that enable seamless partner onboarding, integration, and ongoing operations. Your primary role will be to ensure efficiency, scalability, and compliance while aligning with the team’s mission of delivering exceptional partner experiences.

What You'll Do

- Design, develop, and implement internal business processes - examples include document change management system and system for collecting subjective customer feedback

- Map out existing processes to understand their flow and identify inefficiencies

- Identify process bottlenecks and inefficiencies, and recommend solutions for continuous improvement

- Collaborate with the Product, Enterprise Systems, Customer Success, and engineering to implement workflows

- Monitor process performance, track key metrics, and report on process outcomes

- Document and maintain up-to-date process workflows, guidelines, and SOPs

What You'll Bring

- Experience in project management, operations, or related roles, preferably in a fast-paced or complex environment

- Proven track record of working with product, engineering, and customer success teams to align processes with business goals

- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills to drive collaboration and alignment

- Practical experience in analyzing, mapping, and reengineering workflows

- Ability to gather, analyze, and interpret data to inform process improvements and measure success

- Strong organizational skills to manage multiple initiatives and ensure process documentation is comprehensive and accessible

- Reliable vehicle access to travel to our test sites

- Willingness to travel 1-2 times to out of state commercial sites

This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from (January 2027 - April 2027). Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position.

About Us

SharkNinja is a global product design and technology company, with a diversified portfolio of 5-star rated lifestyle solutions that positively impact people’s lives in homes around the world. Powered by two trusted, global brands, Shark and Ninja, the company has a proven track record of bringing disruptive innovation to market and developing one consumer product after another has allowed SharkNinja to enter multiple product categories, driving significant growth and market share gains. Headquartered in Needham, Massachusetts with more than 4,100 associates, the company’s products are sold at key retailers, online and offline, and through distributors around the world.

AI at SharkNinja

At SharkNinja, we’re building an AI-native culture. We’re not waiting for the future; we’re creating it. Our people are expected to experiment boldly, adopt new tools, and continuously raise what’s possible to create meaningful impact for our consumers. If you believe the best way to do your job hasn’t been invented yet, you’ll fit right in.

Join the SharkNinja Early Edge Experience: Built for early career talent. Geared toward impact. Driven by speed. Whether you’re in a co-op or internship, our early talent program is designed to provide valuable exposure to the industry and a fast-paced professional environment. You’ll dive into meaningful projects and tasks that sharpen your skills and deepen your knowledge. Along the way, you’ll benefit from professional development opportunities, community events, and connections that make your experience well-rounded and enriching. Your time with us will culminate in an opportunity to showcase your contributions and learnings to SharkNinja leaders because this is a program for those ready to shape what’s next — fast.

Are you passionate about using your technical skills to bring bold ideas to life? Do you thrive in fast-paced environments where innovation and impact go hand in hand? Are you excited by the challenge of building — and breaking — the next generation of high-performance consumer products? If so, we invite you to learn more about the Engineering & Technology Intern at SharkNinja.

This is a single application for engineering and technology early talent opportunities across SharkNinja. The hiring teams are spread across our electrical, embedded, software, robotics, digital, quality, test, and safety functions.

Whichever team you join, you’ll work alongside experienced engineers on products that reach millions of homes. You might be bringing up a new circuit board, tuning a control algorithm on a robot, writing cloud or mobile code for a connected appliance, building a test rig that runs thousands of cycles, investigating a field return, or helping keep our products and facilities safe and compliant. If you’re technically curious, hands-on, solution-oriented, and ready to make an impact from day one, we want to hear from you!

Teams that you can be connected to through this posting include:

- Electrical Engineering (Shark and Ninja)

- Electrical Design Engineering, Advanced Development

- Firmware & Embedded Software Engineering

- Control Systems & Algorithms

- Robotics & Mechatronics

- Software Engineering

- Web Development (CodeShark)

- Mobile App Development

- Software & Technical Program Management

- Digital & Website Technology

- IT Service Desk

- Product Test Engineering

- Software Quality Assurance & Test Automation

- System Quality Assurance (Robotics)

- CORE Quality (Consumer, Operational, Regulatory & Engineering)

- Product Safety & Regulatory Compliance

- Environmental Health & Safety (EHS)

Here are some of the EXCITING things you’ll get to do:

- Contribute to the design, development, and validation of next-generation Shark and Ninja products — and the software that powers them

- Work hands-on in labs, at the bench, and in code: building prototypes, test fixtures, scripts, and tools that engineers actually use

- Support debugging, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and failure investigation on real products and real consumer data

- Develop and execute test plans, document results, and turn data into recommendations that shape design decisions

- Participate in design reviews, sprints, stand-ups, and technical discussions alongside experienced engineers

- Collaborate cross-functionally with Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Design, Firmware, Quality, Operations, Marketing, and Product Management

- Gain exposure to the full product development lifecycle — ideation and prototyping through certification, mass production readiness, and post-market consumer feedback

- Own a meaningful project end to end and present your contributions to SharkNinja leaders

Depending on the team, your day-to-day may include:

Electrical, Embedded & Robotics

- Designing, simulating, and evaluating analog and digital circuits — power supplies, signal filtering and amplification, motor control, sensor integration, battery management — using tools such as LTSpice and Altium

- Board bring-up, debugging, and validation of real-time embedded electronics, including serial communication protocols such as I2C, SPI, and UART

- Writing and debugging firmware in C/C++ for microcontrollers and prototyping on platforms such as Arduino or Raspberry Pi

- Developing classical (e.g., PID) and advanced (e.g., MPC) control algorithms in Python, MATLAB, or C++ and tuning them on real hardware

- Working with robotics and navigation technologies such as LiDAR, Time-of-Flight sensors, and SLAM/V-SLAM

- Supporting EMC, safety, and certification testing, EBOM/CBOM cost analysis, DVT, and DFMEA

Software, Digital & IT

- Building and verifying cloud and connected-product software on the AWS IoT platform using TypeScript and Python

- Developing cross-platform mobile apps in React Native, TypeScript, Swift, Kotlin, or Rust that communicate with devices over BLE, Wi-Fi, MQTT, and RESTful APIs

- Front-end and web development, CMS content updates, analytics and performance tracking, and UX audits supporting SharkNinja’s websites

- Testing and evaluating AI-powered digital features such as chatbots, smart search, and content recommendation engines

- Coordinating technical roadmaps, schedules, dependencies, and risks across hardware, firmware, and app teams using Agile, Scrum, and JIRA

- Providing first-level IT support — device setup and imaging, account provisioning, ticket management in tools such as ServiceNow or Zendesk, and meeting room technology

Quality, Test, Safety & Compliance

- Designing and building custom electro-mechanical test rigs and automated test systems that simulate real-world consumer use

- Writing automated test scripts in Python or C++ and integrating sensors, microcontrollers, and data acquisition tools into test setups

- Executing manual and system-level test protocols for products, robots, and mobile apps, and documenting defects in JIRA or similar tools

- Tearing down SharkNinja and competitor products, analyzing large data sets with statistical tools, and investigating failure modes

- Evaluating consumer field returns, star reviews, and call center feedback to drive root cause analysis and corrective actions

- Supporting product safety and regulatory compliance work, internal audits, risk assessments, EHS inspections, and safety training aligned to standards such as OSHA and EPA

ATTRIBUTES & SKILLS:

- Education: Current student in a related bachelor's or master’s or PhD program or has graduated from such a program within the past year

- Must be able to work a full-time, 40-hour-per-week schedule

- Pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics or Mechatronics, Quality Engineering, Information Technology, Environmental Health & Safety, or a closely related technical field

- Strong fundamentals in your discipline — and the curiosity to apply them to problems you haven’t seen before

- A builder’s mindset: comfortable with lab and test equipment (oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies, data loggers), hand tools and prototyping, a code editor, or all of the above, depending on your focus

- Programming or scripting experience in one or more of C, C++, Python, MATLAB, TypeScript, JavaScript, Java, Kotlin, or Swift

- Able to read and interpret schematics, technical drawings, and product requirements

- A natural communicator who can explain complex technical topics clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, in writing and out loud

- Strong attention to detail in testing, documentation, and data analysis; offers data-backed insights and constructive feedback

- Comfortable multitasking and shifting between immediate tasks and longer-term projects in a fast-paced environment, with proactive ownership of your work

- Collaborative, positive, and eager to contribute to an innovation-driven team

- Proficient in Microsoft 365, particularly Excel and PowerPoint

- Prior internship, co-op, capstone, club, research, or personal project experience in consumer products, electronics, robotics, software, or quality is a strong asset

Any of the following are a plus — we don’t expect all of them:

- ECAD, CAD, or simulation tools; PCB layout; surface mount soldering; quick-turn prototyping

- Knowledge of IoT ecosystems, embedded systems, or connected consumer hardware

- Cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, or Firebase; Git version control

- Bipolar and CMOS technologies, power electronics, BLDC motors, and EMI mitigation

- Knowledge of the Software Development Life Cycle and/or Software Testing Life Cycle; Agile, Scrum, and JIRA; the CSQE Body of Knowledge

- Testing methodologies such as sanity, regression, exploratory, and negative testing

- Analytics and data visualization tools such as Google Analytics, Hotjar, Power BI, or Tableau

- Familiarity with safety and environmental regulations (OSHA, EPA) and risk assessment methodologies

- UI/UX tools such as Figma and exposure to design-thinking workflows

- Ticketing and remote support tools, device imaging, and Windows/macOS administration

Location: Remote (US / Canada)
Duration: Fall/Winter 2026 co-op — 8 months, flexible start September 2026
Level: Graduate student (MS or PhD, returning to your program after the co-op)

About Apollo

Apollo leads Block's efforts to build the Customer World Model (CWM): a continuously evolving representation of each customer's goals, context, history, constraints, and likely future needs.

The CWM powers proactive intelligence across Block's ecosystem. Instead of customers navigating products in search of features, intelligence observes their world, understands what matters, anticipates what comes next, and initiates actions on their behalf.

We believe the next generation of AI products will not be defined by chat interfaces or isolated agents. They will be defined by rich world models that enable systems to reason over a customer's evolving state, make better decisions, and learn continuously from outcomes. Apollo designs, prototypes, and guides the development of this intelligence layer.

About the role

We're hiring a small cohort of graduate research interns to help build the foundations of proactive intelligence.

This is not a traditional internship. You'll own a research problem end-to-end: framing the question, developing methods, running experiments, publishing findings, and, when successful, shipping your work into production systems used by millions of customers and sellers.

You'll work at the intersection of representation learning, foundation models, reinforcement learning, causal reasoning, agentic systems, and product intelligence. The goal is not simply to build smarter models, but to build systems that develop a deeper understanding of customers and use that understanding to make better decisions over time.

Past interns have shipped production systems within months and published their work in the same year.

What you'll work on

Depending on your interests and Apollo's roadmap, you'll focus on one or more of the following areas:

Customer World Models

Building rich representations of customers from event streams, financial activity, operational signals, and behavioral data.

Examples include:

- Representation learning over long-horizon customer histories

- Event-based foundation models

- Multi-modal customer representations spanning structured, sequential, and graph data

- Memory architectures for long-term customer understanding

Proactive Intelligence

Developing systems that can anticipate customer needs and initiate helpful actions before being asked.

Examples include:

- Opportunity detection and next-best-action systems

- Long-horizon planning and decision-making

- Preference and goal inference

- Learning when intervention creates value versus friction

Agentic Decision Systems

Building agents that reason over customer world models and take actions in real environments.

Examples include:

- Tool use and planning

- Multi-step reasoning over customer state

- Autonomous workflow execution

- Recovery and adaptation under uncertainty

Learning from Feedback Loops

Developing methods that allow intelligence to improve continuously from real-world outcomes.

Examples include:

- Reinforcement learning from customer and product feedback

- Reward modeling and preference learning

- Counterfactual evaluation

- Credit assignment over long decision horizons

Evaluation and Measurement

Building evaluation frameworks that predict real-world performance, trust, and customer value.

Examples include:

- Simulated customer environments

- Longitudinal evaluation

- Decision quality metrics

- Safety and reliability benchmarks

What we're looking for

We're looking for researchers interested in building systems that understand people, learn from experience, and improve over time.

Required

- Currently enrolled in an MS or PhD program in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, Mathematics, Operations Research, or a related field, and returning to that program after the co-op.

- Strong foundations in modern machine learning, including deep learning, optimization, representation learning, and foundation models.

- Experience conducting independent research and translating ideas into working systems.

- Fluency in Python and experience with PyTorch, JAX, or similar frameworks.

- Evidence of research excellence through publications, open-source contributions, technical leadership, or equivalent work.

Nice to have

- Experience with large language models and agentic systems.

- Experience with reinforcement learning, reward modeling, or sequential decision-making.

- Experience with representation learning for structured, temporal, or graph data.

- Familiarity with large-scale training and production ML systems.

- Interest in building AI systems that directly affect customer outcomes.

What you'll get

- Direct mentorship from researchers working on the future of proactive intelligence at Block.

- Access to large-scale datasets, modern infrastructure, frontier models, and substantial compute resources.

- Opportunities to publish and contribute to open-source projects.

- A chance to shape foundational technology that could power the next generation of Block products.

- Exposure to both scientific research and product deployment, with a clear path from idea to impact.

Application Guidelines

Candidates may submit up to 9 active applications within a 60-day period. Reapplications to the same role are accepted 90 days after a previous application has been reviewed.

Use of AI in Our Hiring Process

We may use automated AI tools to evaluate job applications for efficiency and consistency. These tools comply with local regulations, including bias audits, and we handle all personal data in accordance with state and local privacy laws.

Contact us here with hiring practice or data usage questions.

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and into the real world. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. Today, we're deploying autonomous systems on heavy construction equipment across the country, improving safety on job sites and accelerating schedules on critical infrastructure projects.

We're not here debating the future of AI. We're deploying it in the real world. In just two years, we've raised $350M and achieved the first fully autonomous excavator deployments in construction.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

About the Role & Team

As a Sensor Hardware Test intern, you'll work alongside our test engineering team to characterize and validate the sensors - cameras, lidar, and supporting hardware - that power Bedrock's autonomous excavators. You'll help build test fixtures, run structured lab test campaigns, and turn raw sensor data into clear conclusions that guide how we select and integrate hardware. You'll also get out to our field site to see how bench results hold up on a live construction machine. You’ll own a hands-on project involving sensor hardware testing end-to-end, and your results will directly shape what hardware ends up on the next generation of machines.

What You'll Do

- Build and iterate on test fixtures and benchtop setups - mechanical mounts, wiring harnesses, DAQ integration - used to characterize camera, lidar, and other sensor hardware

- Run structured sensor test campaigns in the lab, following defined test procedures and capturing repeatable, well-documented data

- Help safely deploy test setups and instrumentation out at our field site, and support live field test campaigns on active construction equipment

- Develop tools to automate data collection, process raw sensor logs, and summarize results against pass/fail criteria

- Help scope and select test equipment (light meters, targets, DAQ hardware, valves and actuators for environmental or fluid test rigs) for new test setups

- Support electrical and mechanical debugging of test hardware, including wiring, sensor interfacing, and basic CAD work for fixture design

- Document test methods, results, and findings, and present conclusions to the test engineering team to inform sensor selection and system design decisions

What We're Looking For

Required

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, Optics, Mechatronics, or a related field

- Hands-on experience building or testing hardware through coursework, personal projects, or a prior internship

- Working proficiency in Python for data processing, scripting, or automation

- Comfortable with basic lab equipment and electrical debugging (multimeters, oscilloscopes, DAQ systems)

- Comfortable working outdoors and around active construction equipment, and willing to spend time on-site at our field test location for deployment and field testing

- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to document technical work clearly for a team

Preferred

- Exposure to cameras, lidar, radar, or other sensing hardware through coursework, internship experience, or personal projects

- Experience with CAD tools for mechanical fixture design

- Familiarity with Git and working within a shared codebase

- Prior coursework, internship, or project experience in robotics, autonomous systems, or controls

We are seeking Software Engineering Interns to work on the Fab team for the winter term. The internship begins in January, with a preferred commitment of 4 to 8 months. You will build full-stack applications, tools, and infrastructure for a software-defined semiconductor fab.

The software you build will help engineers develop and operate the fab. If you’re excited by building complex features from scratch, and learning new domains quickly, this is a great place to grow.

Our philosophy is to get things built and tested in days or weeks, not months. Because of this, a portfolio (can be your GitHub) is required to apply: show us the things you’ve actually built! For us, a good portfolio includes evidence of software engineering excellence and curiosity.

- Solid understanding of systems fundamentals: memory, performance, concurrency

- Experience building non-trivial software projects from scratch (personal, academic, or professional)

- Interest in one or more of the following areas: databases, visualization, data processing pipelines

Nice-to-have

- Experience with interactive software such as Figma, Blender, CAD tools, KiCad, or scientific computing environments

- Understanding of collaborative or distributed systems (e.g., CRDTs, OT, WebSockets)

- Appreciation for texts such as Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs and Designing Data-Intensive Applications: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems

Product Intern — Fall

About Hubs

At Hubs, we're building the intelligence layer for organizations — where anyone can build AI solutions that spread and compound across the org. Our team is growing, fast-moving, and ambitious — led by multi-exit Silicon Valley entrepreneurs with a strong track record of creating products that shape how people work.

Joining Hubs means working on problems that matter. You'll be building for yourself, your peers, and millions of professionals navigating the shift from pre-AI to AI-first work. The products you create will be visible, widely used, and part of a broad societal transformation in how knowledge work gets done.

About the Role

As we prepare for launch, we're looking for a Product Intern to work directly with the founders at the intersection of product, users, and implementation. This role is for someone who wants hands-on exposure to how an AI product gets shaped, validated, and brought to life for its earliest users.

You'll help us understand how the product behaves in the real world, spot what's working and what isn't, and turn those signals into decisions that make the product better. Along the way, you'll support how we deliver solutions to our first customers — sitting close to both the product and the people using it.

What You'll Do

- Shape the product — Dig into how the platform works, test real use cases, and surface what matters most for a great user experience.

- Analyze and structure — Turn product data, user feedback, and testing signals into clear insights that inform what we build next.

- Validate quality — Help ensure the product is reliable and ready for users by catching edge cases and prioritizing the issues that count.

About Base

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.

About the Role

Base designs its own hardware, builds it in its own factory, installs it at homes, and sells the power. That vertical integration is our advantage, and it means the suppliers we choose and the deals we strike directly shape our cost and speed.

As a GSM Intern, you will own sourcing for a set of assigned parts, run the RFQ process end to end, and negotiate cost and terms directly with suppliers.

This is not a shadowing internship. You will be given parts to source, suppliers to negotiate with, and quotes that carry real weight in our build cost. The work sits between Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, and Finance, and suits someone who thinks in systems, is comfortable acting on incomplete information, and likes building durable, repeatable sourcing processes.

What You’ll Do

- Own sourcing for a set of assigned parts: build and run RFQs, compare supplier quotes on cost, lead time, and capacity, and make the call on award.

- Negotiate price, payment terms, and lead time directly with suppliers, and track savings against the prior baseline.

- Build supplier cost models — bottoms-up where you can — so you can tell a fair quote from a padded one.

- Support qualification of new suppliers and second sources for critical components: gather quotes, samples, and capability data for the team’s decision.

- Track supplier performance — cost, delivery, and quality — and flag risk before it hits the production line.

What You’ll Bring

- Working toward a degree in supply chain, industrial engineering, operations, mechanical engineering, business, or another quantitative field — or on a comparable path.

- Strong spreadsheet skills and comfort working with large, messy datasets. SQL, Python, or scripting is a plus.

- Genuine interest in how physical products get built. Exposure to an MRP or ERP system (Odoo, SAP, NetSuite) is a plus, not a requirement.

- Clear, direct written communication — you will send RFQs, quote comparisons, and escalations to suppliers and internal teams.

- Bias to action and follow-through. You close loops without being asked twice.

- Available to work in person in Austin, TX for the duration of the internship.

About the Team

Global Supply Management owns every part that goes into a Base battery and its associated systems. This includes sourcing, planning, and getting it to the line on time. We are ramping in-house manufacturing of our own battery product while qualifying second sources for critical components, which means the plan changes often and the cost of being wrong is a stopped line. Sourcing is where that pressure lands first: the team decides who we buy from and on what terms, and builds the leverage and systems that make those calls repeatable.

Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.

Our Values

- First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

- Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

- Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

- Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

- Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

- Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

- Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.

Do the best work of your life at Base.

OpenGov is the leader in AI and ERP solutions for local and state governments in the U.S. More than 2,000 cities, counties, state agencies, school districts, and special districts rely on the OpenGov Public Service Platform to operate efficiently, adapt to change, and strengthen the public trust. Category-leading products include enterprise asset management, procurement and contract management, accounting and budgeting, billing and revenue management, permitting and licensing, and transparency and open data. These solutions come together in the OpenGov ERP, allowing public sector organizations to focus on priorities and deliver maximum ROI with every dollar and decision in sync. Learn about OpenGov’s mission to power more effective and accountable government and the vision of high-performance government for every community at OpenGov.com.

About the Role

OpenGov is looking for Product Engineer Interns who are eager to learn what it means to own a product — from customer discovery through delivery. This internship is built around a new kind of role born from AI's ability to handle execution work that once required multiple specialists. What AI cannot do is decide what matters, talk to customers, make the right call in ambiguous situations, or own whether a product succeeds. That is what Product Engineers learn to do — and this internship is where that journey starts.

This role is first and foremost about developing product thinking — not becoming a developer. The best interns will be the ones who grow genuinely curious about customers: who they are, what they actually need, and what outcomes depend on solving their problems. The engineering side — using AI-native tooling to write code, build interfaces — is a skill you will be introduced to and encouraged to develop. It is a career accelerator, not a day-one requirement.

If you have a background or strong interest in product management, UX design, engineering, or some combination — and you want real ownership of a problem rather than a slide deck — this internship is for you.

"Product Engineer" is two words — but the first word is the one that matters most. The second is how you get there.

The 10-week internship will run from June 7, 2027 through August 13, 2027.

What You'll Work On

- A scoped product problem: a defined set of customers, problems, and outcomes — sized for a 10–12 week engagement with real impact.

- Customer discovery: you will conduct or observe customer conversations and translate what you learn into product decisions.

- User experience flows: you will define interaction patterns within an existing design system and validate them with users.

- AI-assisted delivery: using AI-native tooling, you will move from intent to spec to working prototype — supported by your team, but accountable for the output.

- Metrics: you will define what success looks like for your area and track it throughout the internship.

How AI Works in This Role

AI-native tooling handles a significant portion of what product managers and designers have historically spent their time on. As an intern, you will be hands-on with these tools from day one:

- Spec writing: AI drafts the first spec from your intent statement. You learn to review, sharpen, and own what gets built.

- UX design: AI generates mockups from the design system based on your flow definitions. You make the product decisions within it.

- Research synthesis: AI clusters and themes interview notes and support data. You interpret what it means and make the call.

- Release content: AI generates release notes and enablement materials from shipped features. You review and refine them.

- Test coverage: AI generates test cases from acceptance criteria. You learn to write criteria precise enough to verify.

What AI does not do: understand your customers, make the call on what matters, own the outcome, or build the cross-functional trust that makes things ship. That is the job — and what you will be learning.

Key Responsibilities

- Participate in customer discovery conversations; synthesize what you hear into defensible product decisions.

- Define user experience flows and interaction patterns within the existing design system.

- Write intent documents that AI tooling can execute against; review AI-generated specs for accuracy and completeness.

- Partner with your engineering and product mentor to resolve ambiguity in real time during the development cycle.

- Track adoption and usage metrics for your scoped area; use them to drive iteration.

- Present your product area and findings in a final intern showcase — covering the customer problem, what you built, and what you would do next.

- Surface gaps, risks, and unanswered questions proactively; don't wait to be asked.

Qualifications & What We're Looking For

- Currently pursuing a degree in computer science, information systems, product design, HCI, business, or a closely adjacent field — or equivalent self-directed experience.

- Genuine curiosity about customers and why products succeed or fail; you find yourself asking "who is this for and does it actually solve their problem?"

- Strong written communication: you can articulate a product decision clearly enough that an engineer and a designer walk away aligned.

- Comfort with ambiguity and speed: you make reasonable decisions with incomplete information rather than waiting for certainty.

- Willingness to grow into code fluency using AI-native tooling — you don't need to arrive as a developer, but you must be willing to get there.

- Prior exposure to product management, UX design, software development, or customer research is a plus — in any form (coursework, projects, prior internships, side work).

- Familiarity with design tools (Figma, etc.) or development tooling is welcome but not required.

Compensation

Boston, MA: $30 per hour

On target ranges above include base plus a portion of variable compensation that is earned based on company and individual performance.

The final compensation will be determined by a number of factors such as qualifications, expertise, and the candidate’s geographical location.

Why OpenGov?

A Mission That Matters.

At OpenGov, public service is personal. We are passionate about our mission to power more effective and accountable government. Government that operates efficiently, adapts to change, and strengthens public trust. Some people say this is boring. We think it’s the core of our democracy.

Opportunity to Innovate

The next great wave of innovation is unfolding with AI, and it will impact everything—from the way we work to the way governments interact with their residents. Join a trusted team with the passion, technology, and expertise to drive innovation and bring AI to local government. We’ve touched 2,000 communities so far, and we’re just getting started.

A Team of Passionate, Driven People

This isn’t your typical 9-to-5 job; we operate in a fast-paced, results-driven environment where impact matters more than simply clocking in and out. Our global team of 800+ employees is united in our commitment to challenge the status quo. OpenGov is headquartered in San Francisco and has offices in Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Dubuque, Dallas, and Pune.

A Place to Make Your Mark

We pride ourselves on our performance-based culture, where every employee is encouraged to jump in head-first and take action to help us improve. If you have a great idea, we want to hear it. Excellent performance is recognized and rewarded, and we love to promote from within.

Benefits That Work for You

Enjoy an award-winning workplace with the benefits to match, including:

- Comprehensive healthcare options for individuals and families

- Flexible vacation policy and paid company holidays

- 401(k) with company match

- Paid parental leave, wellness stipends, and HSA contributions

- Professional development and growth opportunities

- A collaborative office environment with weekly catered lunches.

California Privacy Notice

We are recruiting outstanding Research Interns to work on autonomous vehicles, robotics, and physical AI! Intelligent machines that can perceive, reason, and safely interact with people and the physical world are rapidly becoming a reality. Self-driving cars, autonomous delivery and construction vehicles, mobile manipulators, and other robotic systems are moving closer to widespread deployment. However, fundamental research challenges remain before these systems can operate safely, reliably, and autonomously in complex, unfamiliar environments.

For example, how can we:

- Develop new training paradigms that use perception and interaction to train autonomous vehicle and robot policies in closed loop?

- Equip autonomous systems with online and offline assurances that meet the requirements of safety-critical applications?

- Enable vehicles and robots to navigate across new environments, tasks, and embodiments?

- Build systems that reason under uncertainty and interact safely and naturally with people and other agents?

These are some of the exciting questions being explored by NVIDIA’s Autonomous Systems and Physical AI Research (ASPIRE) group. Our diverse, interdisciplinary team conducts foundational research spanning foundation model design, embodied reasoning, safety, closed-loop training and evaluation, and agentic workflows for Physical AI development. We also investigate related areas including decision-making under uncertainty, deep learning, reinforcement learning, simulation, and the verification and validation of safety-critical AI systems. Our focus is on fundamental research, and lab members are encouraged to publish their work and open-source their code. NVIDIA is known for its collaborative culture, and our researchers work closely with experts across the company in autonomous vehicles, robotics, perception, simulation, and machine learning. This creates opportunities to influence real-world products while retaining the freedom and bandwidth to conduct groundbreaking, publishable research.

What you’ll be doing:

- Designing and implementing cutting-edge techniques for autonomous vehicles, robotics, and physical AI.

- Conducting original research and publishing your results.

- Collaborating with research colleagues, internal product teams, and external researchers.

- Transferring technology you’ve developed to relevant product groups.

What we need to see:

- Currently pursuing a PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

- Relevant research experience in autonomous vehicles, robotics, embodied AI, or autonomous systems.

- Strong knowledge of the theory and practice of vehicle or robot autonomy—or expertise in a related area, with a strong interest in applying your work to autonomous systems.

- A track record of research excellence, demonstrated through publications at leading conferences and journals—such as RSS, ICRA, CoRL, IJRR, NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, TAC, etc.—and through other research artifacts such as open-source software.

- Exceptional Python programming skills; experience with C++ and parallel programming, such as CUDA, is a plus.

- Experience with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch.

- Strong communication and interpersonal skills are required, along with the ability to thrive in a dynamic, research-focused team.

Are you intellectually curious, collaborative, and motivated to solve complex problems at the intersection of AI and the physical world? If so, you may be a great fit for NVIDIA.

Our internship hourly rates are a standard pay based on the position, your location, year in school, degree, and experience. The hourly rate for our interns is 38 USD - 94 USD.

You will also be eligible for Intern benefits. ​

We are creating devices that enable a bi-directional interface with the brain. These devices allow us to restore movement to the paralyzed, restore sight to the blind, and revolutionize how humans interact with their digital world.

Team Description:

The Robot Optics Team is passionate about shaping the future of operating rooms. We are responsible for all optical engineering aspects of Neuralink surgeries, including working on our surgical robotics, supporting operating room equipment, and manufacturing custom consumables. The core device we work on is the robotic system that performs implant insertions. Key subsystems include 2D and 3D machine vision cameras, optical coherence tomography, and surgical site illuminators.

Our team oversees the entire product lifecycle of all optical subsystems across multiple robot versions, from ideation and design through production, testing, and maintenance. We also design hardware for producing and inspecting consumables, such as laser-machined needle cartridges. As we manufacture a significant portion of our hardware in-house, our core activities include bring-up testing, designing hardware acceptance testers, and overseeing manufacturing processes.

Job Description and Responsibilities:

As a Robot Optics Intern at Neuralink, you will build, characterize, and calibrate optical and optomechanical systems used directly in our surgical robots and associated consumables manufacturing systems. These systems are responsible for everything from sub-micron conventional imaging to laser scanning imaging to non-imaging optical power delivery. In this role, you will be expected to:

- Design and simulate optical imaging systems

- Test, verify, and maintain vision systems in robots

- Repair and troubleshoot existing optical subassemblies

- Test and verify optics consumables

- Develop image acquisition and processing software

- Conduct preliminary tests of new imaging technologies for robotic surgeries

- Collaborate with engineering teams to evaluate and implement process improvements

- Prepare relevant documentation and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for robot optics

- 1+ years of relevant industrial experience with assembly, precision alignment, and integration of complex optomechanical systems

- 1+ years of experience with benchtop testing, performance characterization, and metrology benchmarking of optical systems

- Experience documenting and following procedures in the optical design pipeline (e.g., assembly, characterization, verification) with a high level of detail

- Strong understanding of engineering first principles

- Education in an engineering-related field

- Experience with data analysis and image processing

- Experience with optics alignment and optics bench testing

- Experience with fiber optics fabrication

None required. However, if your assignment is longer than 179 days cumulatively within a calendar year, you must go through the Personal Identity Verification process. This process includes completing an online background investigation form and receiving approval of the background check.

National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA)

The 2025 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), Section 3112, generally prohibits citizens of China, Russia, Iran and North Korea without dual US citizenship or legal permanent residence from accessing specific non-public areas of national security or nuclear weapons facilities. The restrictions of NDAA Section 3112 apply to this position. To be qualified for this position, Candidates must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112.

External applicant(s) selected for this position must pass a post-offer, pre-employment drug test. This includes testing for use of marijuana as Federal Law applies to us as a Federal Contractor.

Wireless and Medical Devices

Per the Department of Energy (DOE), Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory must meet certain restrictions with the use and/or possession of mobile devices in Limited Areas. Depending on your job duties, you may be required to work in a Limited Area where you are not permitted to have a personal and/or laboratory mobile device in your possession. If you use a medical device, which pairs with a mobile device, you must still follow the rules concerning the mobile device in individual sections within Limited Areas. Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities require separate approval. Hearing aids without wireless capabilities or wireless that has been disabled are allowed in Limited Areas, Secure Space and Transit/Buffer Space within buildings.

All current job openings are displayed on the Career Page under “Find Your Job” of our website. If you have encountered a job posting or have been approached with a job offer that you suspect may be fraudulent, we strongly recommend you do not respond.

California Privacy Notice

What you will be doing as an Asset Protection Risk Intelligence Intern:

Building the analytical foundation for how Meijer identifies retail crime and fraud risk before loss occurs. Asset Protection receives signals from a wide range of technologies — and today those signals are largely reviewed independently rather than through a single risk lens. This role brings them together. Work includes profiling and joining data across platforms, defining with investigators what a credible early risk indicator actually looks like, building a working prototype that surfaces stores, markets, or offenders showing converging signals, and validating those findings against closed cases. The intern will also develop the measurement framework that shows what prevented loss is worth.

The intern may also get exposure to other activities of the function, including:

- Organized retail crime, fraud, and internal investigations
- Asset protection technology evaluation and pilot governance
- Data privacy and governance considerations for surveillance technologies
- Law enforcement and prosecutor partnership work
- Remote Operations Center and alert response operations
- Broader understanding of Meijer's Asset Protection organization

- Coursework or project experience with Python, R, or SQL, and with a visualization tool such as Power BI or Tableau
- Familiarity with anomaly detection, pattern recognition, or machine learning concepts — exposure is expected, expertise is not

- Ability to work flexible shifts (primarily days) to gain exposure to the full operation of the business

- Drive for results - moves work forward with limited direction and a defined scope
- Customer focus - dedicated to meeting expectations of internal and external customers
- Relationship Skills - can create positive working relationships with customers, team members, leadership, and other internal and external constituencies
